articles.title: Canadian Oil Discount Exceeds $30 Amid Gulf Coast Pressures
articles.excerpt:
(Bloomberg) -- Heavy crude oil in Alberta has weakened to the lowest price relative to US futures in more than four years.

Western Canadian Select’s discount — also called a differential — in Alberta grew to $31 a barrel compared to a monthly average of West Texas Intermediate as of Tuesday, the widest since October 2022, General Index prices show.

On the US Gulf Coast, Canadian heavy crude’s discount expanded to $23.50, the largest in data stretching back to 2018, according to Link Data Services.

The gap is being driven by a supply build-up in the Gulf of Venezuelan imports and high tanker rates that make exporting oil expensive.

articles.title: UBS Sees $110 Brent by Year-End as Gulf Flows Stay Below Prewar Levels
articles.excerpt:
UBS Sees $110 Brent by Year-End as Gulf Flows Stay Below Prewar Levels

UBS has raised its Brent forecast for the second time this month and now expects crude to trade at $110 a barrel at the end of 2026, up from 100. The Swiss bank also lifted its 2027 curve by $5 a barrel at each point, to $95 for March, $90 for June and $85 for September.

“Uncertainty around our forecasts remains elevated, reflecting the unpredictable nature of the Middle East conflict, and the pace of recovery in Gulf production and global oil demand,” UBS said in a note.

On October 6, UBS raised its fourth-quarter forecast to $100 from about $80 and its 2026 average to 491.57 from 483.74.
